memory_update.text: For transmission_interconnection_construction, the most direct US-listed contractor universe includes PWR, MYRG, MTZ, and PRIM; PWR appears the cleanest large-cap mapping and MYRG appears more focused but smaller.

Equipment and component suppliers to track for grid/substation buildout include GEV, ETN, HUBB, POWL, VMI, and potentially AZZ; these require margin and product-mix verification rather than assuming pure transmission exposure.

Engineering, permitting, and software/data candidates for the same node include J, ACM, BSY, and ITRI; these are generally second-order exposures and should be scored lower unless utility/grid project evidence is found.

The key Serenity falsification checks for this node are whether reported backlog is truly grid/transmission/substation-related, whether contracts protect margins from labor/material inflation, and whether utilities/developers delay projects despite high demand because of permitting or rate-case constraints.

Need a follow-up screen for smaller US-listed niche suppliers in transformers, HVDC components, protection relays, grid cybersecurity, vegetation management, ROW acquisition, and interconnection software; some may be below the preferred USD 1B market-cap filter or embedded inside larger conglomerates.

node: Transmission buildout, interconnection, substations, utility construction and grid services
summary: Expanded US-listed universe for the grid bottleneck node. The strongest direct exposures are specialty utility construction and engineering contractors with transmission, distribution, substation, grid-hardening, undergrounding, and interconnection execution capabilities. Second-order exposures include electrical equipment, grid hardware, power-control systems, poles/structures, software, and metering providers that can benefit when utilities, renewables developers, hyperscalers, and industrial loads must spend on grid capacity before generation or load growth can be monetized. This is research universe expansion only, not a buy/sell list.
